findings.summary: F1 from the prior round (d3ba6c6) is NOT actually fixed. The replacement regression test 'does not false-positive on a brain-only commit when invoked from a subdirectory' is STILL vacuous — for a different structural reason than the original — because it never lands a commit after the pinned handoff, so `git rev-list -1 --before=$since HEAD` resolves the anchor to HEAD itself (self-diff, always empty) regardless of whether root-resolution or the exclude pathspec work at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Verified via two independent, real mutations on src/stop-reminder.ts (each applied, tested, and reverted): (1) replacing `root = execFileSync('git',['rev-parse','--show-toplevel'],...)` with `root = cwd` (deleting the F1 fix entirely) — full suite still 31/31 green, including this exact test. (2) replacing `:(exclude)${brainRel}` with a pathspec matching nothing (`:(exclude)DOES_NOT_EXIST_MUTATION`) — full suite still 31/31 green, same test included. Root cause: the test's only two commits are a pre-handoff baseline and the handoff-landing commit itself (dated exactly `since`); `--before` is inclusive of that exact second, so `anchor === HEAD` always, making the diff a trivial self-diff no matter what pathspec or cwd is used. I then wrote a genuinely non-trivial variant (a later commit landing OUTSIDE the invocation subdirectory, after the handoff) and confirmed it DOES discriminate: with root-resolution removed it wrongly returns false (a real false negative — a merged PR at the repo root would be silently missed when the hook runs from a subdirectory); with the original code it correctly returns true. So the underlying implementation is correct for this property, but the shipped test proves nothing about it — exactly the ADR-0070 §3 bar ('a proof that can't fail proves nothing') the prior round's F1 was about, recurring in the fix commit meant to close it. The commit message's claim that mutation testing 'confirmed' the property (attributing insensitivity to 'path.relative + git's own cwd-relative pathspec resolution compose correctly') is technically observed-true for this one test but mischaracterizes the cause (anchor==HEAD triviality, not pathspec-resolution equivalence) and is misleading about what got locked in.

findings.summary: B3 has no self-silencing mechanism short of writing an entirely new pinned handoff, breaking the 'self-silencing without session state' contract pattern RFC-011/ADR-0034 established for the sibling B1 nudge (the review charge explicitly asks to check conformance against this pattern). Once `handoffStale` is true, it stays true — and re-fires on literally every subsequent Stop-hook turn, this session and every future session — until someone records a fresh handoff, with no threshold, backoff, or 'declined once' memory.
findings.failure_scenario: RFC-011 §B calls the per-turn-nag risk of a naive Stop nudge out explicitly ('a naive Stop nudge would nag from turn 1 onward... survivable only with strong gating') and ADR-0034 mitigates it for B1 via a strong-signal threshold plus self-silencing the moment ANY handoff/next entry is recorded THIS session. B3 (src/stop-reminder.ts:96-98) is deliberately NOT gated on uncommittedWork and has no threshold at all — the existing passing test 'true when a non-brain commit landed after the pinned handoff' (test/stop-reminder.test.ts:212) is itself empirical proof that ANY subsequent commit unconditionally flips handoffStale to true, with no allowance for whether that commit is the same session's own already-anticipated work (e.g. the exact autonomous-merge-after-writing-a-handoff sequence this repo's own CLAUDE.md standing workflow performs routinely). A mid-session agent that reasonably declines the nudge ('not wrapping up yet, nothing new to report') will see the identical STALE_HANDOFF_REMINDER on every following Stop-hook turn for the rest of the session — a live regression of exactly the failure mode RFC-011 named and ADR-0034 was built to avoid for the sibling mechanism. STALE_HANDOFF_REMINDER's copy ('Before wrapping up, record a fresh handoff') also lacks HANDOFF_REMINDER's explicit 'if you are still mid-session, ignore this and finish normally' escape clause, so there is no in-band signal that declining is safe.

Investigated per the task's explicit prompt (item 5): is the git rev-list/diff machinery bounded/cheap for an extremely long-since-stale handoff? Built a 3001-commit scratch repo via git fast-import with the boundary at the very oldest commit (the worst case: maximum commits between the stale handoff and HEAD). `git rev-list -1 --before=<old-date> HEAD` completed in ~9ms; `git diff --quiet <oldest> HEAD -- . :(exclude).vfkb` over the full 3000-commit range completed in ~4ms. Both are cheap because git's commit-graph walk and tree-diff are metadata/tree operations, not content or per-commit log walks — this is NOT the same class of problem the P1/F5 `--name-only` buffering fix addressed (that was about captured stdout size, not walk cost). Ruled out as a live concern at this scale; not verified at repo sizes several orders of magnitude larger.

Investigated per the task's explicit prompt (item 5, correctness hunt). Constructed a scratch repo with a stale handoff, then `git checkout --detach HEAD`, and called handoffIsStale() directly against it: returned `true` correctly, no crash. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git rev-list`, and `git diff` all function normally in detached HEAD (none require a symbolic branch ref), so this is not a live gap.

Investigated per the task's explicit prompt (item 5). src/engine.ts supersededIds() (L331-335) just builds a Set of every refs.supersedes value with no existence check against real entry ids; isInjectable()'s `superseded?.has(e.id)` is a plain Set lookup. A refs.supersedes pointing at a nonexistent id is inert (matches nothing, no exception, no injectability change) — not a crash surface.

Investigated per the task's explicit prompt (item 5). isHandoff()/isInjectable() only inspect tags/zone/status/provenance/validity, never author/role/session metadata, so a B2 auto-generated fallback handoff (role=executor, tags=[handoff,next,auto]) is picked up by newestHandoffTimestamp() exactly like an agent-authored one — consistent with engine.ts's own latestHandoff() used by resume/brief, which makes the same non-distinction. No special-case gap found.
